sentences.text: Facts of the present case are that the petitioner was working in the post of Pump Operator, as he was appointed vide order dated 16.08.1996.

An FIR was lodged against the petitioner for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 420, 408, 409, 467, 468, 471, 201 & 34 of IPC at the Police Station-City Kotwali, Mungeli, District Mungeli (C.G.) and he was arrested on 25.06.2024.
The petitioner preferred bail application before this Court and the same was allowed vide order dated 16.10.2024.
The Chief Municipal Officer, Municipal Council Mungeli vide order dated 28.06.2024 placed the petitioner under suspension according to the provisions of Chhattisgarh Civil Services (CCA) Rules, 1966.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has been placed under suspension vide order dated 28.06.2024 and four months have lapsed but till date, the order of suspension has not been revoked.

He would further submit that the matter is squarely covered with the judgment passed by this Court in a bunch of writ petitions leading case being Writ Petition (S)
No.9074 of 2023 (Kishore Kumar @ K. Kumar versus State of Chhattisgarh & Others) has decided the issue.

entities.text:
Writ Petition (S)
No.9074 of 2023 (Kishore Kumar @ K. Kumar versus State of Chhattisgarh & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would also submit that the petitioner may be permitted to make a representation before the respondent authorities and the authorities may be directed to consider the representation so made.
4. Learned State Counsel admits the fact that the case of the petitioner is squarely covered by the judgment passed in the case of Kishore Kumar (supra).
He further submits that if the petitioner makes a representation, the grievance of the petitioner would be considered by the concerned authority strictly in accordance with the law.
5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties, perused the order of suspension and other material/documents available on the record.

6. Taking into the consideration the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ajay Kumar Choudhary Vs. Union of India through its Secretary and Another passed in Civil Appeal No.1912 of 2015, this Court in the case of Kishore Kumar (supra) has accordingly held as under:-
"Analysing the language expressions including the punctuation used by their Lordships, categorically stated that the main clause, being mandatory and the two sub-clauses, distinctly marked with the help of the punctuation semi colon (;) and the insertion of the conjunction 'if' to being with the two sub-clauses, clearly indicate that the direction in entirety is continuous in nature and contained within 90 days essentially.

entities.text: Ajay Kumar Choudhary Vs. Union of India through its Secretary and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it clearly shows that the currency of suspension order should not extend beyond three months if within this period the memorandum of charges/charge sheet is not served on the delinquent officer/employee.
Meaning thereby, serving of memorandum of charges/charge-sheet within 90 days of suspension is mandatory.
Further, it is also clear that if the memorandum of charges/charge sheet is served, a reasoned order must be passed for extension of the suspension.

In view of this Court, in Ajay Kumar Choudhary Versus Union of India through its Secretary, (2015) 7 SCC 291, the intent of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is clear that ifthe memorandum of charges/charge-sheer served, an order of extension Ramkumar Mahilang vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151089542/
2 of the suspension must also be passed."

sentences.text:
7. Taking into consideration the facts of the present case, the present petition is disposed of granting liberty to the petitioner to make a representation before the respondent authority in light of the judgment rendered by this Court in the matter of Kishore Kumar (supra) and in turn, the respondent authority is directed to consider and decide the representation of the petitioner within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
8.
Accordingly, this petition stands disposed of.
